questions.question: Explain the concept of Bayesian inference. Define prior distribution and posterior distribution. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Bayesian inference – Explanation - 2 marks
  • Prior distribution - Definition - 2 marks
  • Posterior distribution – Definition - 2 marks
  • Points for reference
  • Bayesian inference - updates the probability as more data becomes available;
  • incorporates prior knowledge; Bayesian Inference is applied in spam filtering, clinical
  • trials, portfolio optimization, etc
  • Prior - represents knowledge about an unknown parameter before observing the data;
  • Informative Priors; Uninformative (Flat) Priors
  • Posterior – is the refined belief; is the probability distribution of the parameters given
  • the observed data

questions.question: Explain the basic working principle of the k-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) classification method. Discuss its strengths and limitations. / [CO2] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Working principle of the k-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) classification - Correct
  • explanation 6 Marks
  • Strengths and limitations – At least 2 each – 4 Marks
  • Points for reference
  • Working Principle
  • • classifies new observation based on the classes of the k closest observations in
  • the training dataset
  • • similar observations tend to belong to the same class
  • • Steps
  • o Select the value of k
  • o Measure distance
  • o Identify nearest neighbours
  • o Assign class
  • Strengths and limitations
  • • Strengths - Simple to understand and implement; No explicit training phase;
  • making it flexible; can model complex class boundaries; Effective when decision
  • boundaries are irregular.
  • • Limitations - Computationally expensive for large datasets; sensitive to noise and
  • outliers, especially for small k; Performance depends on the choice of k and
  • distance measure; affected by feature scaling, requiring normalization.
